title: Implicit interfaces and the small-interface pattern

videos.script: Lesson 26 met an interface in passing, fmt.Stringer, and used it for one sentence. This lesson is about interfaces themselves. {{shapes}} A function asks for a shape, and two unrelated types pass. Neither one says it is a shape. Nothing in Go ever says that. {{writers}} Then one call, fmt.Fprintf, writing to a file, a buffer and a string builder. Three packages that never heard of each other, and one interface they all fit. {{small}} Then size. Most interfaces in the io package have one method. You will count them. A function that asks for one method can be handed almost anything. {{checks}} Last, what happens when a type does not fit. The compiler says which method is missing, or which one has the wrong type. And one line, written once, makes it say so early. By the end, you can write a function that accepts anything able to do what it needs.
